Tune model and preprocessing settings by forecast accuracy

Source: R/model-tune.R
mt_tune.Rd

mt_tune() evaluates every combination of settings in grid by how well it forecasts the last years of data (an inner backtest) and returns the scores and the best specification. tuned() wraps the same procedure into a model specification: each time it is fitted (for example at every origin of an outer mt_backtest()), the tuning uses only the training data it receives, so the selection never sees the years being forecast. The chosen model is then fitted to all training data.

Usage

mt_tune(
  spec_fun,
  grid,
  data,
  prep = NULL,
  inner_origins = 3,
  inner_h = 5,
  metric = "crps",
  n_draws = 100,
  strategy = c("full", "two_stage"),
  target = c("rate", "life_expectancy", "asr"),
  select = c("min", "one_se"),
  by = NULL
)

tuned(
  spec_fun,
  grid,
  inner_origins = 3,
  inner_h = 5,
  metric = "crps",
  n_draws = 100,
  label = "Tuned model",
  strategy = c("full", "two_stage"),
  target = c("rate", "life_expectancy", "asr"),
  select = c("min", "one_se"),
  by = NULL
)

Arguments

spec_fun

A function that returns a model specification (or list(spec = , prep = )) from named arguments, for example function(order) hyndman_ullah(order = order).

grid

A data frame of settings (columns match the arguments of spec_fun), ordered from the simplest to the most complex setting for select = "one_se".

data

An mt_data object.

prep

Preprocessing pipeline used by every candidate (when spec_fun returns specifications only).

inner_origins

Number of inner origins (1 for a single hold-out).

inner_h

Horizon of the inner backtest (the number of years held out from each origin).

metric

"crps", "wis", "mae", "rmse" or "mase".

n_draws

Draws per inner forecast.

strategy

"full" evaluates every row of grid; "two_stage" first evaluates a coarse grid (every second value of each column, including the first and the last) and then the rows of grid within one step of the best coarse combination in every column. For large grids, such as Tucker ranks, this needs far fewer fits.

target

"rate", "life_expectancy" or "asr".

select

"min" or "one_se".

by

Stratum variables: tune each group of strata separately.

label

Display name.

Value

mt_tune(): a list with scores (one row per setting and group: the settings, the score, its standard error se and whether it was selected), by_horizon (scores by forecast horizon), best (the chosen specification; with by, a list per group), best_prep (the preprocessing of the chosen setting), chosen and origins. tuned(): a model specification; its fit carries tuning (the scores) and tuning_choice.

Details

Design. Each candidate is refitted at inner_origins consecutive origins and forecasts inner_h years from each; the last origin is inner_h years before the end of the data. inner_origins = 1 is a single hold-out: fit to the years up to T - inner_h and forecast the last inner_h years (with inner_h = 5 or 10, the usual choice of smoothing and model parameters for demography::fdm()). Several origins average over more periods and make the choice depend less on the events of one period (Tashman 2000).

What can be tuned. spec_fun receives one row of grid as named arguments and returns a model specification, or list(spec = , prep = ) to tune preprocessing together with the model: for example the smoothing parameter of step_smooth(), the fitting window of step_window() and the number of components of hyndman_ullah(). Preprocessing is given either by spec_fun or as prep.

Criterion. metric is computed for target: the log death rates of the observed cells ("rate"), life expectancy at birth ("life_expectancy", years) or the log age-standardised rate ("asr"), per test year and stratum. "crps" and "wis" score the whole forecast distribution; "mae" and "rmse" the error of the median (point accuracy); "mase" scales the absolute error by the mean year-to-year change of the training data (rates only).

Selection. select = "min" takes the lowest score. select = "one_se" takes the first row of grid whose score is within one standard error of the lowest (the one-standard-error rule of Hastie, Tibshirani and Friedman 2009, Section 7.10), so order grid from the simplest to the most complex setting. The standard error comes from the mean scores per origin and stratum (per test year for a hold-out of a single stratum); these blocks are correlated, so it is approximate and tends to be too small. With few test years, differences between settings are often within this error: the selection is then uncertain, and scores shows it.

Groups. With by, the strata are split by these stratum variables and each group is tuned and fitted on its own (for example women and men with their own number of components). A joint model such as li_lee() then pools only within each group.

References

Tashman LJ (2000). Out-of-sample tests of forecasting accuracy: an analysis and review. International Journal of Forecasting 16(4): 437-450.

Hastie T, Tibshirani R, Friedman J (2009). The Elements of Statistical Learning, 2nd edition. Springer, New York.

Examples

x <- mt_example(deaths = "single", years = 1990:2012)
tn <- mt_tune(function(drift_window) rwd(drift_window = drift_window),
              data.frame(drift_window = c(5, 10, 20)), x, inner_origins = 2, inner_h = 3)
tn$scores
#>    drift_window       crps          se selected
#>           <num>      <num>       <num>   <lgcl>
#> 1:            5 0.06098906 0.003459354    FALSE
#> 2:           10 0.05295919 0.003492327    FALSE
#> 3:           20 0.04738829 0.003376065     TRUE
# a single hold-out of the last 5 years, tuning the smoothing too
smoothed_lc <- function(lambda) {
  list(spec = lee_carter(), prep = mt_prep(step_smooth(lambda = lambda)))
}
tn2 <- mt_tune(smoothed_lc, data.frame(lambda = c(1, 100)), x, inner_origins = 1, inner_h = 5,
               metric = "rmse", n_draws = 50)
tn2$scores
#>    lambda       rmse          se selected
#>     <num>      <num>       <num>   <lgcl>
#> 1:      1 0.06871123 0.007634507    FALSE
#> 2:    100 0.06770156 0.007473598     TRUE
